rows.answer: Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) is currently in a Neutral regime with a Panic Index of 47.1, so no threshold-driven exposure change is indicated. Over the selected period, the strategy returned 19.2%, compared with 61.4% for Buy & Hold, while maximum drawdown moved from -35.1% to -35.1%. In this sample, the strategy underperformed Buy & Hold on both return and drawdown dimensions. The return gap is consistent with lower market participation: average exposure was 59.8%, while reduced exposure coincided with approximately 161.1 percentage points of uncaptured positive market return versus 128.5 points of downside cushion on an arithmetic attribution basis. This suggests the panic-side accumulation rule may be more useful than treating greed as a symmetric exit trigger in this sample. The next diagnostic step is to test drawdown attribution, market-regime performance, threshold sensitivity, and risk-adjusted metrics.
